pages.ja:
そうして、彼女は残された。
もう戦う意味のない少年。
マスターでなくなった者が危険を冒し、元凶である自分が安息に浸っている。
その事実が、彼女の心を一層深く沈ませる。

pages.en:
And so she was left behind by a boy who had no reason left to fight.

No longer a Master, he was placing himself in danger while she—the cause of it all—rested here in comfort.

The knowledge dragged her heart deeper still.
pages.mirrorMoon:
And she is left alone.
There is no reason for the boy to fight.
The one who is no longer a Master walks into danger while she, the danger’s cause, is resting.
That fact depresses her even more.

pages.ja:
「彼は森に向かいました。
後悔しているのですか、サクラ」
従者は自らの主に問う。
彼女は頷くことなく、憂いげに瞳を細め、一度だけ首を横に振った。

pages.en:
“He has gone toward the forest. Do you regret it, Sakura?”

The attendant put the question to her master.

She did not nod. Her eyes narrowed in sorrow, and she shook her head just once.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“He has headed to the forest.
Do you regret it, Sakura?”
The servant asks her master.
The girl does not nod, but narrows her eyes and shakes her head once.

pages.ja:
「……後悔なんて出来ないでしょう、ライダー。そんなもの、今さらなんの意味もない」
「そうですね。確かに、意味のない質問でした」
「ええ。けど、辛いことだけじゃない。わたしね、不謹慎だって分かってるのに嬉しいの。先輩がわたしのために何かしてくれるのは、純粋に嬉しいから」
そう言いながらも、彼女の顔は苦悩に満ちていた。
嬉しいと呟く口は、罪の意識で縫い付けられたように重い。

pages.en:
“…Regret isn't even possible now, Rider. What meaning could it have this late?”

“No. You are right. It was a pointless question.”

“Yes. But it isn't all painful. I know I shouldn't feel this way, but I'm happy. When Shirou does something for me, it simply makes me happy.”

Even as she spoke, anguish filled her face.

The lips that whispered of happiness felt heavy, as though guilt had sewn them shut.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I can’t regret it, Rider. There’s no point now.”
“You are correct. That was certainly a meaningless question.”
“Yes. But it’s not all painful. I know it’s wrong to say this, but I’m happy. I’m happy that Senpai’s doing something for me.”
But her face is filled with agony.
The mouth that says she’s happy is heavy as if bound by a feeling of guilt.

それに、なにより
」
これ以上戦いに参加されては困る。
それは自分にも彼にも、良くない未来を持ってくるだろう。

pages.en:
“But it's wrong. Grandfather won't show him any mercy. As long as Shirou keeps fighting, his life will always be in danger.

“And more than anything—”

She could not allow him to remain part of this battle.

It could only bring a dark future for them both.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But that’s wrong. Grandfather will show no mercy. As long as Senpai keeps fighting, there’s a chance that he’ll die.
And most of all
”
It’s troubling for her if he stays in the war any longer.
It will bring a bad fate down upon them both.

pages.ja:
だからこそ戦いを止めさせ、彼には日常に戻ってほしかった。
どうせ自分は長くない。
それならせめて、彼にだけは生きていてほしい。
……だが。
そう願う反面で、希望に縋る自分がいるのだ。
彼が戦う事で、もっと一緒に居られるのなら。
いや、愛する者が自分のために傷ついてまで戦ってくれる事が、どれほど悦ばしい事か。

pages.en:
That was why she wanted him to stop fighting and return to his ordinary life.

She herself did not have long to live.

If nothing else, she wanted him to survive.

…And yet.

Even as she wished for that, another part of her clung to hope.

If his fighting meant they could stay together a little longer—

No. How could it not delight her, to know that the person she loved would fight for her even if it meant being hurt?
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s why she wants him to simply return to his normal life.
She will not last long.
That being the case, she wants him to live.
…But…
At the same time, she clings to hope.
For as long as he fights, she can be with him.
No, it delights her that the person she loves is fighting and getting hurt for her sake.

pages.ja:
戦ってほしくはない。
けれど、戦ってくれる事が嬉しすぎる。
二つの願望は対立し、互いを受け入れないまま拮抗する。

pages.en:
She did not want him to fight.

But the fact that he would filled her with far too much joy.

The two desires stood opposed, neither yielding to the other.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She doesn’t want him to fight.
But having him fight makes her happy.
The two contradictory wishes compete for control within her.

pages.ja:
「……嘘。拮抗なんて、してないくせに」
苦しげに漏らして、彼女は自らの暗部を思い知る。
そう。
本当は戦ってほしい。自分を助けてほしい。今まで振り向いてもらえなかった分、何倍も応えてほしい。
その為なら
彼が傷ついてもいい、と。
彼女は、思ってはならない事さえ、思ってしまった。

pages.en:
“…Liar. They aren't evenly matched at all.”

The words escaped her in pain, forcing her to confront the darkness inside her.

Yes.

The truth was, she wanted him to fight. She wanted him to save her. After all those years when he had never looked her way, she wanted him to answer her feelings many times over.

Even if it meant he was hurt.

She had allowed herself to think the one thing she must never think.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…What a lie. It’s not competing at all.”
With a pained murmur, she acknowledges the darkness within her.
Yes.
She wants him to fight. She wants him to save her. She wants him to answer her to make up for all the times he did not.
For that reason
he can get hurt.
And she thinks about something she shouldn’t.

体内の虫が、彼女の暗い情念に応えるように神経を這う。
……たった一瞬。
たった一度、傷ついた彼の姿を想像しただけで、虫たちは彼女の体を侵していく。

“Hah… ngh…!”

She clutched her chest.

The worms inside her crawled along her nerves as though answering the darkness of her desire.

…It had been only an instant.

She had imagined him wounded only once, and already the worms were overrunning her body.
pages.mirrorMoon:

She clutches her chest.
As if responding to her dark passions, the worm within her stirs against her nerves.
…It was only for an instant.
She imagined him getting hurt for a mere instant, and the worm has begun to violate her once again.

じくじく。
じくじくじく。
体内で蠢く耳鳴りがする。

わたしの体は醜く、こんな事で興奮するほど邪だ。

体内で生じ、意識ごと呑み込むうねり。

pages.en:
Throb.

Throb.

Throb, throb, throb.

She could hear their writhing inside her like a ringing in her ears.

She felt the chill coursing through her, dissolved into her blood.

My body is hideous—so perverse that something like this can arouse me.

…The worms dissolved in her blood, becoming a sweet poison that set her body aflame.

A surge born within her, swallowing even her mind.

And amid that ever-mounting fever, she always had the same thought.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Wriggle, wriggle.
Wriggle, wriggle.
Wriggle, wriggle, wriggle.
The squirming in her body makes her ears ring.
It melts into her blood, causing a chill to run through her body.
The feeling stimulates her, and she thinks her body is
lewd
filthy
and evil.
…The worm that melted into her blood becomes
aphrodisiac,
a sweet poison,
heating up her body.
The waves threaten to wash her consciousness away.
She always thinks with her heated head.

それは神経に絡みついたモノと何も変わらない。

pages.en:
These arms and legs are so thoroughly defiled that they no longer seem human.

Her body stumbled over its dark yearning and fell at once, groveling shamelessly against the ground.

Her breath would not stop. Her spine melted in aching pleasure, like some viscous thing.

She was no different from the things entwined around her nerves.

The harder she tried to deny them, the deeper the worms burrowed into her nerves, melting her mind into mire, until—

—she felt that she herself had become a worm.

In the end, that sinister illusion ruled every inch of her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That her limbs are too dirtied to be called human limbs.
Sexual desire
Bitter longing
easily fills her body, and she clings on the ground in a vulgar manner.
Her panting does not stop, and her
hips wriggle
spine feels
like mucus.
It is no different from the thing entangling her nerves.
The worm violates her nerves the more she tries to deny it, her consciousness is melted away, and…
She feels like she is a worm herself.
And in the end, an ominous feeling dominates her whole body.

“…Yes. I don't have long anyway.

“I'm lucid right now, but if I let my guard down, I lose track of what I was doing. …My memories grow hazier by the day, and I can't feel my arms or legs. Even my sense of time has fallen apart. A single day won't stay whole for me anymore.

“…Even this morning. Somehow, it feels as though a week has passed since I saw Shirou off.”

…Like today. It feels like it’s been a week since I saw Senpai off.”

…She had accepted her death.

And even as she fought what she saw as the ugliness within her that still clung to hope, she begged Rider to protect him.

She forced herself to smile.

The black-clad Servant answered with only a nod, then turned her back on her master.

“…Yes. The truth is, I think so too.”

The words came from her almost like a song.

Her earlier gloom had vanished. There was even something graceful in the way she held herself as she said,

“But don't worry, Rider.

“After all, that man can't defeat me.”

She gave a soft laugh.

And smiled like a girl plucking a flower.
